name: TCPDump — Fundamentals, Switches & File I/O
description: TCPDump is a command-line packet sniffer that captures and interprets network traffic using libpcap. Requires root/sudo. Supports live capture and reading from PCAP files. Key switches modify verbosity, output format, name resolution, and file I/O. Combine switches for best results: -nnvXX for full output without resolution.
source: CDSA Module 07: Intro to Network Traffic Analysis
notes:
=== INSTALLATION & VALIDATION ===
which tcpdump                          # check if installed
sudo apt install tcpdump               # install if missing
sudo tcpdump --version                 # verify version
man tcpdump                            # full documentation

=== KEY SWITCHES ===
-D        List all available interfaces
-i eth0   Select interface to capture from
-n        Do not resolve IP addresses to hostnames
-nn       Do not resolve IPs or port numbers
-e        Include ethernet (layer 2) header in output
-X        Show packet contents in Hex + ASCII
-XX       Same as -X but also includes ethernet header (= -Xe)
-v        Verbose output (more protocol detail)
-vv       More verbose
-vvv      Maximum verbosity
-c 100    Capture only 100 packets then exit
-s 0      Capture entire packet (no truncation)
-S        Show absolute sequence numbers (default: relative)
-q        Quiet — less protocol info
-A        Show only ASCII (no hex)
-l        Line-buffer output (enables pipe to grep)
-r file   Read from PCAP file
-w file   Write capture to PCAP file

=== COMMON SWITCH COMBINATIONS ===
sudo tcpdump -i eth0                   # basic live capture
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nn              # no name/port resolution
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -e               # include MAC addresses
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -X               # hex + ASCII output
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nnvXX           # full detail, no resolution
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -c 50 -nn        # capture 50 packets

=== FILE I/O ===
# Write capture to file (output doesn't scroll terminal)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w ~/output.pcap

# Write with no resolution + verbose
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nvw /tmp/capture.pcap

# Read from file
sudo tcpdump -r ~/output.pcap

# Read file with full detail switches
sudo tcpdump -nnSXr /tmp/capture.pcap
  # -nn = no resolution, -S = absolute seq nums, -X = hex+ASCII

# Read ASCII only (pipe-friendly)
sudo tcpdump -Ar telnet.pcap

# Pipe to grep (requires -l for line buffering)
sudo tcpdump -Ar http.cap -l | grep 'mailto:*'

=== TCPDUMP OUTPUT FIELDS ===
Timestamp  | Protocol | Source.Port > Destination.Port | Flags | Seq/Ack | Options | Length
Example:
10:58:33.719241 IP 172.16.146.2.55260 > 172.67.1.1.https: Flags [P.], seq 1953742992:1953743073, ack 2034210498, win 501, length 81
  → Timestamp: 10:58:33.719241
  → Source: 172.16.146.2 port 55260
  → Destination: 172.67.1.1 port https (443)
  → Flags: [P.] = PSH + ACK
  → seq/ack: TCP sequence/acknowledgment numbers
  → length: payload bytes

=== TCP FLAGS IN OUTPUT ===
[S]    SYN  — connection request
[S.]   SYN-ACK — server response
[.]    ACK  — acknowledgment only
[P.]   PSH+ACK — data push with ack
[F.]   FIN+ACK — connection teardown
[R.]   RST  — reset (abrupt close)
